body.statement: For the Clopper--Pearson preliminary region \(C_n\), profile discrepancy \(\Delta_n\), and Berger--Boos calibration in \(\operatorname{pv}_n\), \(P_{\vartheta}\{\tau(\vartheta)\in K_n\}\ge1-\alpha\) at every sample size for every \(\vartheta\) in either design. The bound holds along arbitrary sequences approaching \(\mathfrak D\), including point-to-set transitions. Uniformly over compact subsets of \(\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\) that are locally saturated in the following explicit sense---there is a common neighborhood of each \(\zeta\) on which, for observable coordinate \(q\), the compatible target correspondence is the finite union of the incident graphs \(t=F_\chi(q)\), with no additional observable equality restriction---one has \(\sqrt n\,d_{\mathrm H}(K_n,W_n)\xrightarrow{P}0\). On those locally saturated strata the profile boundary and the Wald ellipse have the same first-order quadratic expansion and \(\chi^2_{2,1-\alpha}\) calibration. At a law with a non-singleton identified set, without the separated-chart conditions, or on a lower-dimensional observable chart, the theorem asserts coverage only and makes no claim that \(\operatorname{diam}(K_n)\) shrinks or that \(K_n\) is first-order equivalent to \(W_n\).
body.justification: Exact preliminary coverage and discrete-tail calibration prove finite-sample causal-target coverage without rank stability; a direct quadratic proof recovers Wald geometry on locally saturated separated charts.
body.gap: Lower-dimensional observable charts add a model-fit quadratic to the saturated-likelihood deviance, so separation and target covariance alone cannot imply the originally claimed universal Hausdorff equivalence.
body.consumer: Boundary-sensitive PN/PS analyses receive honest uncertainty without mistaking a nonshrinking or model-fit-sensitive confidence fiber for point identification.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(q_0\) denote the true observable law, including the independent margin law in design A when it is sampled, and put \(t_0=\tau(\vartheta)\). By the definition of the corresponding full fiber and target set,
\[
t_0\in\mathcal T(q_0). \tag{28}
\]
Each multinomial cell count is marginally binomial. A two-sided Clopper--Pearson interval inverts its two exact binomial tail tests, so its two noncoverage tails are bounded by their allocated probabilities. Bonferroni's inequality over all selected-table and independent-margin cells therefore gives
\[
P_{q_0}\{q_0\notin C_n\}\le\beta_n. \tag{29}
\]
No rank, compatibility-neighborhood, or identification condition is used here.

For a fixed compatible pair \((q,t)\), define
\[
G_{q,t}=P_q\{\Delta_n^{\mathrm{rep}}(t)
\ge\Delta_n^{\mathrm{obs}}(t)\mid\Delta_n^{\mathrm{obs}}(t)\}.
\]
The discrete upper-tail lemma applied to the replicate statistic gives
\[
P_q(G_{q,t}\le u)\le u\qquad(0\le u\le1). \tag{30}
\]
On \(\{q_0\in C_n\}\), equations (28) and the supremum in \(\operatorname{pv}_n\) imply
\[
\operatorname{pv}_n(t_0)
\ge\min\{1,\beta_n+G_{q_0,t_0}\}. \tag{31}
\]
Since \(\beta_n\le\alpha/2\), exclusion of \(t_0\) from \(K_n\), together with (29)--(31), yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_{q_0}\{t_0\notin K_n\}
&\le P_{q_0}\{q_0\notin C_n\}
 +P_{q_0}\{G_{q_0,t_0}\le\alpha-\beta_n\}\\
&\le\beta_n+(\alpha-\beta_n)=\alpha.
\end{aligned} \tag{32}
\]
This is a finite-sample statement containing no continuity constant. Applying it at each index of an arbitrary triangular array proves the same bound along sequences approaching \(\mathfrak D\).

We now prove the narrowed first-order assertion rather than importing it from a generic likelihood theorem. Fix a compact locally saturated subset \(K\subset\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\). Write \(I_\zeta=\Omega_\zeta^{-1}\) in reduced coordinates; compact interior positivity makes its eigenvalues uniformly bounded above and below. For \(q=\zeta+h/\sqrt n\), with bounded \(h\), a third-order Taylor expansion of each term \(N_j\log q_j\), with the simplex reference coordinate restored, gives uniformly on \(K\)
\[
2\{\ell_n(\widehat\zeta_n)-\ell_n(q)\}
=n(q-\widehat\zeta_n)^{\top}I_\zeta(q-\widehat\zeta_n)+o_P(1). \tag{33}
\]
The remainder is uniform because all probabilities are bounded away from zero and the finite-alphabet third derivatives are uniformly bounded. The two-sample version is the sum of two such expansions and has the block information corresponding to \(\Omega_\zeta\).

Local saturation says that, in a common ambient neighborhood, the restriction \(t\in\mathcal T(q)\) is the finite union of equations \(t=F_\chi(q)\) over incident charts, with no further equality restriction on \(q\). Their common first derivative is \(J_\chi(\zeta)\), and the \(C^2\) condition gives
\[
F_\chi(q)=\tau+J_\chi(\zeta)(q-\zeta)+O(\|q-\zeta\|_2^2) \tag{34}
\]
uniformly over the finite incident family. Positive definiteness of \(V_\tau=J_\chi\Omega_\zeta J_\chi^{\top}\) makes \(J_\chi\) have row rank two. Local saturation then also places the target in the relative interior of \([0,1]^2\): otherwise a full-row-rank linear image of an ambient neighborhood would cross a boundary of the square. On a compact set the distance from that boundary is uniform. Minimizing the quadratic in (33) subject to the linearization in (34) gives, by the Lagrange-multiplier equations,
\[
\Delta_n(t)
=n(t-\widehat\tau_n)^{\top}
\widehat V_n^{-1}(t-\widehat\tau_n)+o_P(1) \tag{35}
\]
uniformly for \(\|t-\tau\|_2=O(n^{-1/2})\). The common value and Jacobian make the leading term identical on every incident graph; the positive eigenvalue bound makes it uniformly coercive. The same coercivity and (33) show that accepted targets lie in an \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\) neighborhood.

For a replicate generated under any \(q\) in that shrinking neighborhood with \(t\in\mathcal T(q)\), the centered empirical vector has the uniform multinomial normal limit established by the subsequence argument in the separated-Wald proof. Applying the same quadratic minimization to the replicate version of (35) gives a \(\chi^2_2\) limit uniformly in \((q,t)\). Moreover, the Clopper--Pearson region has \(\sup_{q\in C_n}\|q-q_0\|_2=O_P(\sqrt{\log n/n})=o_P(1)\): this follows directly from the binomial likelihood-ratio or Chernoff bound at tail allocation of order \(n^{-2}\), uniformly on the interior compact set. Hence the supremum replicate tail in \(\operatorname{pv}_n(t)\) converges uniformly on the root-\(n\) boundary to the \(\chi^2_2\) upper tail, and \(\beta_n\to0\). Consequently
\[
K_n=
\left\{t\in[0,1]^2:
n(t-\widehat\tau_n)^{\top}\widehat V_n^{-1}
(t-\widehat\tau_n)
\le\chi^2_{2,1-\alpha}+o_P(1)
\right\} \tag{36}
\]
in root-\(n\) Hausdorff scale. Since the eigenvalues of \(\widehat V_n\) are bounded away from zero and infinity with probability tending to one, an \(o_P(1)\) perturbation of the quadratic level moves its boundary by \(o_P(n^{-1/2})\). Comparing (36) with \(W_n\) proves
\[
\sqrt n\,d_{\mathrm H}(K_n,W_n)\xrightarrow{P}0.
\]

The local-saturation qualification is necessary for this particular deviance and Wald pair. If the observable chart has codimension \(r>0\), the quadratic minimization of (33) includes an additional nonnegative model-fit term in the normal directions. The replicate deviance then has \(r+2\), rather than two, first-order quadratic degrees of freedom, and the realized model-fit term changes the root-\(n\) profile radius. The conditions defining \(\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\) control target covariance and chart separation but do not exclude such lower-dimensional rank charts. Thus outside the locally saturated subclass, (32) remains valid but no Hausdorff equivalence to the frozen \(W_n\) is asserted.
